name: auth-workos-jwt
title: Auth — WorkOS AuthKit (bring your own auth)
description: Use WorkOS AuthKit as the identity provider: verify each request's AuthKit access token against your client's JWKS and feed the user, organization, org role, permissions, entitlements and feature flags into ctx.auth / RLS via a resolveIdentity adapter.
docs: Pass `workosIdentity(env)` as `resolveIdentity` in your Worker entry (`createWorker({ resolveIdentity: workosIdentity(env), … })`, or `.extend((env) => ({ resolveIdentity: workosIdentity(env) }))` on the generated app builder). On the client, create the LunoraClient with `authTokenOnUpgrade: true` and call `setAuthTokenProvider(client, fetchToken, { subject: user.id })` from `lunorash/client` (`@lunora/client` without the umbrella), where `fetchToken` returns `getAccessToken()` and maps `LoginRequiredError` to `null`. Guide: https://lunora.sh/docs/concepts/external-auth

envVars.name: WORKOS_CLIENT_ID
envVars.description: Your WorkOS client id (client_…), from the WorkOS dashboard's API keys page. Not a secret — the frontend uses it too.
